texts: salt, cloth sheet, selfish kin
Kin are as salt upon a cloth sheet: bright while the wetness lasts, gone once it has dried.
After my father's business collapsed, the cousins who used to fill our table stopped calling, and I felt like a cloth sheet that was washed and hung up forgotten; write a doha about it.
doha pls: relatives are like salt in a cloth sheet, they stick around as long as there is sweat to soak up
Please write a doha saying that relatives gather around a prosperous man like salt clinging to a cloth sheet, but when the water dries they fall away, and none of them will walk with him to the end.
doha pls: relatives are like the winnowing fan, they keep the grain of your wealth and blow away the husk of your trouble, the chakor waits for its beloved but kin wait for gifts
winnowing fan, chakor, selfish kin
The winnowing fan keeps the grain for itself; kin gather for the grain of your wealth and flee the chaff of your grief, while the chakor, alone, still watches the sky.
My brothers danced at my promotion party and avoided me when I needed money for the operation; write a doha with a winnowing fan and a chakor in mind.

Compose a doha that says the chakor loves its beloved without wanting anything back, but the kin around us love for what they can win, and when the winnowing fan of hardship is shaken they scatter like the husk.
When my business was thriving everyone in the clan was at our gate, but when the furnace of my fortune cooled, I sat alone for months; please write a doha about this.
furnace, selfish relatives
doha pls: the furnace shows who's real, family comes for the warmth and leaves when the metal's cold
In the furnace of fortune the kin gather to bask, and in the cold ember of misfortune not a face is seen.

Please craft a couplet saying that relatives are like those who gather around the furnace for warmth, praising the owner while the heat lasts, and walking away without a word as soon as the fuel is gone.
doha pls: family turns the house into a market the moment money is involved
The market of kinship opens when there is gain, and the house of grief is empty.
The same uncles who haggled over every inch of our house at the market of inheritance did not come to the funeral; write a doha about it.
market, house, kin

Compose a doha showing that family ties in a house are like a market, where each member weighs what he can gain from the other, and when the goods are exhausted, they close up and leave the old man alone.
bee, selfish kin
The bee comes to the flower for honey and leaves once it is sucked dry; so the kin come to the wealthy man.
Please write a doha saying that kin are like bees that gather around a man who has sweetness to give, and when he has nothing more, they swarm off to some other blossom without looking back.
doha pls: relatives are like bees, they buzz around when you have honey and disappear after
My uncle's family hovered around us as long as my father was giving, like bees around a blooming branch, and not one visited when he was sick; please write a doha.
tongue, selfish kin
doha: even family tongues turn bitter when money is on the table
My own brother shouted at me about money over the tongue-lashing of the funeral feast, and I realised blood doesn't always mean love; write a doha.
Sweet is the tongue of the kinsman while the purse is full, and sharp as a blade when it is empty.
Make me a doha that says the relatives who speak so sweetly with their tongue while you are prosperous will speak ill of you when you fall, and none of them will share the burden of your sorrow.
We were on the same boat of debt after my father's illness, but my aunts and uncles took their share of the gold and left us to row alone; write a doha.
doha pls: kin are like passengers on a boat, they ride with you in good times but won't pay for the gold of the journey
boat, gold, selfish kin
In the boat of life the kin sit beside you singing, but in the storm they leap into the water, taking the gold with them.
Write a doha that says family climbs aboard the boat of your good fortune when it is laden with gold, but when it begins to sink every one of them swims for himself, and you alone remain with it.
traveler, family bonds
doha pls: family is just travelers who walk part of the way with you
My dad travelled for work all his life to feed the family, and when he got old and tired, no one wanted to take him in; I need a doha.
Compose a doha that says each person is a traveller who meets wife, sons and relatives along the way, loves them and is loved, but at the time of leaving he must go alone, for no one can go along.
A traveller on life's long road meets kin at every stop, but none will walk the last mile beside him.
At the well of the world the yogi sits and watches the kin draw water for themselves alone.
well, yogi, kin
The yogi who sat by the well in our village told me that my sons and wife cry for me today but they cry for themselves, not for me; please write a doha.

Can you make a doha saying that a yogi sitting by the well sees how every relative draws from the man's wealth and kindness for his own thirst, and he alone knows that no one will carry the man across.
doha pls: a yogi knows family only loves you for what you give, like drawing water from a well
My mother spent forty years at the grindstone feeding the family, and when her hands gave out, the rope of obligation was cut without a thank-you; write a doha about it.
doha pls: family ropes you in with promises, then the grindstone of duty grinds you down
The rope of kinship binds the man to the grindstone of duty, and no kinsman loosens the knot as he is ground down.
grindstone, rope, kin
Please write a doha showing that the rope of family ties holds a person fast to the grindstone of daily toil, and the relatives who benefit from his labour will not take it from him when he is tired.
The chakor loves its beloved for love's sake alone; the kin love the purse, and the purse only.
chakor, selfish love
doha pls: a chakor loves with nothing in return, family doesn't
My daughter-in-law said she loved me like a mother, but only until the will was read; I think of the chakor, who loves with no wish for gain. Write a doha.
Compose a doha that says that the chakor's love asks for nothing, whereas the love of kin is a trade, in which each gives only to receive and stops giving the day he stops receiving.
kin love for gain
doha pls: family only loves you when you're useful

I want a doha that says relatives and household love us for their own convenience, and when we cease to be of use their affection disappears, so the wise do not stake their peace on the warmth of family.
The kin love us for what we bring, not for what we are; blessed is the heart that knows this early.
When I lost my job, my cousins stopped inviting me to their weddings, and I understood, for the first time, whom they had loved; write a doha.
My family stood beside my brother's funeral pyre, and one by one, they went to attend to other matters, leaving me with a snake of loneliness and the ash of his body; write a doha.
snake, ash, kin
Beside the pyre the kin remain only until the ash is cold; the snake of loneliness then crawls into the heart.
Pen a doha saying that when the body turns to ash, the relatives who wept at the pyre return to their affairs, and the soul alone feels the snake-bite of death, with no one to share its pain.
doha pls: family leaves after the ash is cold, and loneliness bites like a snake
doha pls: family walks you to the cremation ground gate and then goes back
Compose a doha that says the family that loved us in life accompanies us only to the cremation ground, where we lie alone, and the one who knows this should not trust in ties that cannot follow.
At my father's cremation, I noticed how fast everyone started chatting about dinner, and I saw that relatives walk with you only to the last gate; write a doha.
Wife and sons follow only to the gate of the cremation ground, and then they turn back to their meals.
cremation ground, kin turn back
inheritance, broken ties
doha pls: family fights over property the moment parents are gone
My brothers and I haven't spoken since our parents died and the property was divided, and I realised love was never what held us; write a doha.
While the parents lived, the sons were brothers; once the will was read, they were rivals.

Please write a doha that says the ties of brothers and sisters often last only as long as the parents' hands hold them together, and when the inheritance is opened, each one pulls his own share and the family tears.
I performed at the family function with all my heart, like a peacock dancing in the monsoon, but when I needed help they all looked away; write a doha.
The peacock dances before his kin in the monsoon, and when the rain is gone, the kin are gone too.
I want a doha saying that kin applaud the peacock's dance as long as it entertains them, but when it can no longer dance, no one in the family stays to listen to its sorrowful cry.
peacock, family
doha pls: the peacock dances for the clan when it is happy, but when it cries, nobody listens
relatives, selfish love
I want a doha that tells us that relatives share our laughter easily, but our tears are ours alone, since everyone is busy with his own concerns, and only the Lord is a constant companion.
I realised who truly cared for me when I was in the hospital: only two out of thirty relatives came; write a doha.
The kin come to the feast, and not to the fast; they sit at the joy, but not at the sorrow.
doha pls: family are fair-weather folk
cloth sheet, fickle kin
My cousins wrapped me in a cloth sheet of praise at my wedding and stripped it away when the dowry was not enough; write a doha.
Compose a doha showing that the love of family is like a cloth sheet thrown over you in good weather, easily drawn back in bad, so a wise person does not depend on it for warmth in the cold.
doha pls: kin cover you with their sheet when it benefits them, pull it away when it doesn't
The kin spread a cloth sheet of love over your head, and take it back before the night is over.
Write a doha saying that the sweet fragrance of family love is like sandalwood: it comes from your own giving, and when the wood is spent, the kin go looking for another to sit beside.
sandalwood, kin
Kin are the sandalwood that lends its scent only while it burns; when the burning ends, they leave no fragrance.
My relatives praised my kindness like sandalwood while I was giving them things, and abandoned me when I stopped; write a doha.
doha pls: relatives are friendly like sandalwood scent, but when you stop giving, the fragrance goes
The kin come like the moth to your glow and shoot like the arrow when you fall.
doha pls: relatives flutter like moths around success and shoot arrows at failure

I'd like a doha showing that kinsmen cluster like moths around the successful, and when failure comes, the same kinsmen shoot arrows of blame, and the unlucky man learns that his true wealth lies not in family.
After the accident, my relatives were quick with advice and slow with help; one arrow of a harsh word from an uncle hurt more than the injury, and a moth of a cousin visited once; write a doha.
arrow, moth, kin
As a traveller I met a rich merchant whose family followed him like an elephant herd, but when he fell ill by the road, all vanished, leaving him with the stranger; write a doha.
doha pls: the family is an elephant's herd that leaves you when you are wounded, traveler
Write a doha that says the kin follow the great like a herd behind an elephant, but when he is wounded and the road turns hard, a traveller gets no help from them and is helped only by strangers.
elephant, traveler, kin
The elephant is followed by a herd when strong; the traveller is left by his kin when weak.
I want a doha that says we spend our whole lives caring for the wife, the sons and the household, yet at the moment of the last journey, none of them can take even a single step along with us.
doha pls: you love your family but they can't come with you at the end
My wife and children are the dearest to me, yet I know none of them can come with me when my time is up; write a doha.
cannot come along
Dearest are the near ones, yet at the last parting not one can take our hand beyond.
Each loves the other for his own sake, and calls it love; peel away the name and the want is bare.
Write a doha saying that the love within a household is mostly for one's own comfort and benefit, that every relationship has some need behind it, and that selfless love is rare and only the Lord's.
self-serving love
I realised in my fifties that my whole family adored me because I was the one who paid; I'd like a doha on what I learned.
doha idea: everyone in the family loves you for their own reasons
Give me a doha showing that a parent is like a needle that joins the whole family together with its own piercing, and that, after the stitching is done, the family forgets the needle and moves on.
My grandmother stitched every wedding dress in the family with her one needle, and at her death no one remembered who made them; write a doha.
needle, forgotten service
doha pls: a needle stitches for everyone and gets no thanks, like parents
The needle serves all the garments and is forgotten in the corner; so the parent who serves the kin.
doha pls: kin are like a herd of elephants that trample you and herons that wait for what falls out of your hands
At my uncle's funeral some relatives stood like herons waiting for the will to be read, others stamped about like elephants claiming the land; write a doha.
elephant, heron, greedy kin
The elephant takes the field, the heron takes the catch; the kin take whatever the dying man leaves behind.
Write a doha saying that when a man dies, relatives behave like the elephant that tramples the field and the heron that waits to snatch, and none thinks of the departed soul who now journeys alone.
The chakor knows one love, but kin quarrel at the mosque steps for coins.
mosque, chakor, kin
doha pls: the chakor longs for its beloved alone, and kin quarrel even outside the mosque
My cousins fought over the family land outside the mosque, and a chakor seemed more loyal in its longing than they to each other; write a doha.
Compose a doha that says family members who pray together in the mosque may still plot against one another over wealth, whereas the chakor's love is pure, so we should seek the pure love of God.
The priest reads his verses over the pyre, and the kin, like sand, flow away through the fingers of grief.
The priest at my father's funeral said not to cry for the relatives who left early, for they were like sand slipping away; write a doha.

Please craft a couplet that says the priest recites sacred words at the funeral and the relatives stand for a while, but like sand they drain away soon, and only the soul's own deeds go with the departed.
sand, priest, kin
doha pls: kin are like sand, they slip through your fingers, and even the priest can't hold them
forest, family
Compose a doha saying that the family is like a forest in which every creature seeks its own food and shelter, and when a storm arrives, each runs separately, so a wise man trusts only the Lord.
doha pls: family is a forest, everyone is fending for themselves
In the forest of kinship, each creature hunts for its own den; there is none that will carry you across.
I walked through a forest with my cousins and noticed how each of us ran for ourselves at the first sound of danger, and it reminded me of family; write a doha.
I gave my whole youth to my brothers and sisters, and when I finally asked for a small favour, every one of them had a reason to say no; write a doha.
I want a doha showing that a man may spend all his years serving his household, yet the household serves only itself, and at his last hour he finds that he alone must settle his account.
You give your all to the kin, and in your need they count their own.
kin owe nothing
doha pls: family expects everything from you and gives little back
The washerman cleans the garments of all and keeps none; so the dutiful son washes the whole family's stain and keeps no thanks.
doha pls: relatives are like the washerman's laundry, they get cleaned on your effort and go back to someone else
Write a doha that says the dutiful member of a family is like a washerman who works hard cleaning others' burdens, and the family sends him on to the next job without a thought for his weariness.
The washerman in our colony remarked that he cleans everyone's garments but nobody cleans his burdens, which is how my family treats me; write a doha.
washerman, kin
At my mother's deathbed, the whole family was crying, but I saw that not one of them could help her cross over; write a doha.
Death cuts every cord of kinship in a moment; no hand can hold the one who must go.
doha pls: family can't save you from the end
Make me a doha that says all the ties of blood and marriage are strong in life, but at the time of death they cannot lift a finger, and one must go alone on the road that none can share.
death ends all ties
doha pls: everyone you call yours is just on loan
They said mine, mine, mine, and none was ever truly yours; the loan returns to its giver.
I want a doha that says wife, son, brother and friend are all given to us for a little while by the Lord, they are never truly ours, and the one who knows this loves them lightly.
borrowed relations
My grandfather told me on his last day that the people he called his own had never truly been his; write a doha.
doha pls: kids are like pearls, you string them for a night under the stars then they go their own way
The pearls of the household are strung beneath the stars of a night, and by morning each has been given away.

Write a doha saying that children are pearls we polish through the years, and as the night under the stars ends they scatter to their own lives, so the parent who expects company at the end is sorely mistaken.
My daughters sparkled like a pearl necklace at the wedding under the stars, and then went to their husband's families; no one stays with the father at the end, write a doha.
pearl, stars, family
milk, heron, kin
doha pls: relatives drink the milk of your kindness and then act like herons when you're in trouble
My relatives drank the milk of my hospitality for years, and when my husband fell ill, they stood around like herons watching and doing nothing; write a doha.
The kin drink the milk of your goodness, and stand like herons when you need a hand, unmoving.
Compose a doha showing that the household enjoys the milk of a generous man's kindness for long, and when he needs even a drop of help, they stand aside like herons and wait for him to fall.
kin and wants
Everyone in my extended family has a request for me and none have a thought for me; write a doha.
I want a doha that tells the story of the person on whom the whole family depends, who has to give and give, and whom nobody asks how he is, and who learns that love is a one-way street.
doha pls: relatives only call when they need something
The requests of the kin come in a flood; they fall silent when you need them.
fly, thorn, kin
The fly hums about the sweetness; the thorn lies waiting; and the kin make their choices accordingly.
Can you make a doha saying that relatives are like flies who settle on a sweet thing and leave at once if a thorn appears, so a man with only sweetness is surrounded, and he with sorrow is alone.
doha pls: relatives are like flies on a thorn, they swarm for the sweet, but sting when you're sore
Whenever I got a bonus, my relatives swarmed around me like flies, and when I got a thorn in my life, they were all silent; write a doha.
loom, family
doha pls: you work at the loom of life for your family but they won't weave you into their lives
Write a doha saying that a man works at the loom through his whole life weaving comfort and name for his family, but when his own yarn runs out, none of the family will weave him a final warmth.
At the loom of life the father weaves a cloak for all, and in his last cold they have no yarn for him.
My father wove his life like a weaver at the loom to give the family a good name, and at his funeral half the clan didn't show up; write a doha.
doha pls: kids leave when they're grown and parents are alone
The parents are needed while the children are weak; they are alone when the children are strong.
After I retired, my children called on Sundays and my relatives called never; I'd like a doha on how little remains of the household at the end.

I want a doha that says parents toil all their lives to raise their children and build the household, and in their old age the children go off to their own lives, leaving the elders to face the end alone.
parents alone at the end
The priest binds you in seven vows to seven hundred kin, yet at the hour of need all vows are loosed.
The priest at our wedding blessed us with a hundred relatives, and none of them appeared when my wife was in hospital; write a doha.

Please write a doha that says the priest may bless the household with sacred rituals and many relations, but a family bond is only as strong as its benefit, and all rituals are forgotten when the benefit is gone.
priest, kin ties
doha pls: even the priest can't make family love you more than your wealth
Pen a doha showing that kinsmen gather like fish around the bait of wealth or position, and when the bait is eaten, they leave, so a wise man does not mistake their crowd for his own.
We caught fish with my cousins every summer, but when I needed help to carry my father's body, only the fish in the pond seemed to listen; write a doha.
fish, selfish kin
The fish gathers where the bait is, and the kin where the bounty is; both swim away when the bait is gone.
doha pls: relatives are like fish, they come for the bait and swim off when it's gone
It was only after I lost everything that I saw who in my family was real, as if my troubles were a touchstone; write a doha.
The touchstone of misfortune shows which kin are true and which are false.
doha pls: troubles are the touchstone that test your family's love
touchstone, kin
Write a doha that says a hard time is the touchstone on which family bonds are tested, and the relatives who flee in a crisis show themselves for what they are, while rare ones remain.
The touchstone separates the true from the false, and the inn of kinship empties when the evening grows long.
I treated my dwelling like an inn for my relatives and they stayed as long as the food lasted; the touchstone of my illness showed who was true. Write a doha.
Compose a doha showing that family is an inn where each guest rests for a while, and the touchstone of hardship proves who among them is real, since most leave and only a few will remain.
doha pls: the touchstone of time shows the family is only an inn, they stay a night and leave
touchstone, inn, kin
The pot of water is shared while it is full, and left to the thirsty when it is dry; so the kin and our riches.
pot of water, kin
I want a doha that says relatives are like those who drink from a pot of water as long as it is full, and when the pot is cracked and dry they walk on, forgetting the one who filled it.
doha pls: relatives drink from your pot of water when it's full and ignore you when it's empty
My cousins drank from the pot of water at our gate all through the hot months, but none brought a pot when ours ran dry; write a doha.
Compose a doha showing that the household takes the seed of a man's earnings and keeps it, while the winnowing fan of the world blows the husk of his tired self into the wind, to be forgotten.
doha pls: relatives use the winnowing fan on you, take the seed and toss the chaff
The kin take the seed and toss the chaff with the winnowing fan, and the man is left with the husk.
winnowing fan, seed, kin
My sister's family took the seed of my savings and threw away the husk of my care with a winnowing fan; write a doha about it.
I felt lost in a forest of relatives at my own wedding, and when I was in trouble I couldn't find one that would help; write a doha.
forest, kin
In the forest the nests are many, yet the weary bird has no branch to rest on.
doha pls: family is a forest where everyone only cares for their own shelter
Write a doha saying the family is a vast forest in which each creature is occupied with its own survival, and the one who looks for shelter from relatives will be wandering until the end.
The crow at my window cawed louder than my own relatives called, and when a beggar knocked, he alone asked about my father; write a doha.
doha pls: a crow and a beggar showed more care than my family
crow, beggar, family
The crow calls its kin to share a crumb; the kin of men do not call a beggar to their feast.
I'd like a doha showing that even the crow calls its kin to share, and the beggar remembers the one who fed him, yet human families gather only where gain lies and forget the poor and the old.
winnowing fan, kin
The winnowing fan blows the chaff away from the grain, and the kin from the poor man's gate.
Write a doha saying that kin are like chaff in the winnowing fan, present only while there is a harvest, and when the grain is gathered they are blown away by the first breath of difficulty.
After the harvest failed, my relatives, who had been sharing our food, drifted off like chaff from a winnowing fan; write a doha.
doha pls: the winnowing fan blows away the family when the harvest is gone
doha pls: a mirror shows the truth about your family if you look closely
I looked in the mirror after the funeral and saw how old I had grown, and how quickly my relatives had gone; write a doha.
mirror, kin
The mirror shows the face and not the heart; the kin show a smile and not their need.
Compose a doha showing that the mirror of misfortune reveals the true face of one's relatives, who smile while the days are good but turn away their faces from the sad and the needy.
It was my own uncle who cheated me out of my share, and I felt like I had been bitten by a snake I had fed; write a doha.
The snake sleeps in the folds of kinship, and wakes when the inheritance is spoken of.
doha pls: a snake hides in the sleeve of the family, and it bites you when you least expect it
Give me a doha that says the family may hold a hidden snake, the greed that bites those who trust most, and that a man who relies on relatives for his security stands on shaky ground.
snake, kin
The thief robs by night, the kin by day; one steals the purse, the other the peace.
doha pls: relatives are thieves in the household, they steal your time, your money and your peace
My nephew stole from my wallet and my relatives took his side; I realised family was never my shelter. Write a doha.

Write a doha that says there are thieves who enter from outside and there are thieves who sit within the household, who take your time, your wealth and your goodwill, and then speak of love as if nothing was taken.
thief, kin
